title: European Hills & Mounds — balanced strict-gate production research

method.inclusion: Named natural hill, summit or deliberately climbable mound with explicitly public foot access to the upper point, ordinary non-technical terrain, a sharp story, all-high confidence, and editorial score >=19/25 with story and walkability >=4.
method.exclusions: Mountain-grade, exposed, scrambling, private, gated, closed, active-quarry, military, drive-up-only, car-park-only and catalogue-duplicate objectives.
method.dedupe_policy: Normalized candidate names and declared aliases checked globally; every live catalogue coordinate checked at 120 m.
method.copy_policy: w and research_note are machine drafts, not final owner voice. Any production import must remain quality flag d until individual review.
method.source_policy: Two or more relevant sources per included row, including at least one official authority or land manager. Live closures override the dossier.
method.balance_policy: Europe-wide city coverage; the UK and London are deliberately absent from this wave.

included.s: Climb a post-war rubble hill over a buried flak bunker
included.q: Humboldthöhe Volkspark Humboldthain, Gesundbrunnen berlin Germany
included.w: A neighbourhood park path climbs onto a piece of buried Berlin. At the summit, the city opens around a hill built over the remains of a flak bunker.

included.q: Vlaggeduin Zuidduinen, Katwijk aan Zee katwijk Netherlands
included.w: Vlaggeduin rises only 37 metres, yet it is the highest dune in South Holland and a decisive climb above Katwijk's coast. A marked Staatsbosbeheer route crosses the upper sand landscape, while bunkers below preserve the Atlantic Wall's harder history.

included.s: Climb Madrid's lone witness hill from the plain to its geodetic crown
included.q: Cerro Almodóvar Cerro Almodóvar, Vicálvaro–Villa de Vallecas madrid Spain
included.w: Cerro Almodóvar is a classic witness hill: erosion left it standing above Madrid's otherwise flat south-east. Public dirt tracks rise to the summit through ground associated with Palaeolithic flint, giant-tortoise fossils, a Civil War bunker and the 1927 School of Vallecas artists.
included.research_note: Madrid's protection plan identifies the 726 m hill, geological and archaeological values, public green-space programme and prohibition on motor vehicles. A current district cross trail uses mixed paths and tracks to the summit and rates its main 7 km circuit accessible to popular athletes; walkers should use the broad established track rather than the technical timed-ascent line.
